readings: Join fees to orders on fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault, dropping fees with no matching order, and group by orders.timespan. For each group, compute the average of rebrate/feerate, ignoring rows where the ratio is NULL. Define the match count as the number of joined fee-order rows in the group, so an order with several fee records is counted once per fee record. Keep only the groups whose match count is strictly above the average match count across all groups. For those groups, return one row with the average of their average ratios, the sum of their match counts, and the average of (match count minus the cross-group average match count). No rounding.

Join fees to orders on fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault, dropping fees with no matching order, and group by orders.timespan. For each group, compute the average of rebrate/feerate, ignoring rows where the ratio is NULL. Define the match count as the number of distinct orders (distinct orders.recordvault) in the group, so an order with several fee records is counted once. Keep only the groups whose distinct-order count is strictly above the average of that count across all groups. For those groups, return one row with the average of their average ratios, the sum of their distinct-order counts, and the average of (distinct-order count minus the cross-group average). No rounding.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT o.timespan AS timespan,
         AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS match_count
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_mc FROM g
)
SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios,
       SUM(g.match_count) AS total_match_count,
       AVG(g.match_count - m.avg_mc) AS avg_excess_match_count
FROM g, m
WHERE g.match_count > m.avg_mc;
WITH g AS (
  SELECT o.timespan AS timespan,
         AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS cnt
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g
)
SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       SUM(g.cnt) AS total_count,
       AVG(g.cnt - m.avg_cnt) AS avg_diff
FROM g, m
WHERE g.cnt > m.avg_cnt;
